name: Contactless payments and NFC secure element
plain: Lets an app act as a contactless card or key. Open on Android, entitlement gated on iOS.
meaning: Android has allowed host card emulation since 2013. Apple opened it first in the EU in 2024.

android.prompt_ui: Default payment app chooser in Settings
android.note: Host card emulation; no Google approval needed

ios.prompt_ui: Default contactless app setting; Face ID to pay
ios.revocation: Settings > Wallet & Apple Pay > Contactless Payments
ios.note: Opened in the EU with iOS 17.4; NFC and SE APIs in more regions from iOS 18.1

limits.headline: Can act as a contactless card or key on Android freely, but iPhone needs Apple approval
limits.user_action: You choose the app as your default payment app, then tap a reader
can: Answer a payment terminal as a virtual card (Android, once you pick it as default)
Hold transit, access or loyalty credentials without the system wallet
Ask for Face ID to pay on iPhone where Apple allows it
cannot: Become the default payment app without you picking it
Work on iPhone without Apple's entitlement
Work on iPhone in every region; it began in the EU and grew from iOS 18.1
limits.differs: Android has allowed this since 2013 with no approval; iPhone opened it first in the EU in 2024 and in more regions from iOS 18.1.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app act as a contactless card or key, held in the phone's secure chip or in software.

marketing.name: NFC and SE Platform
marketing.pitch: Apple opened the phone's secure tap hardware so approved apps can offer in app tap to pay and keys.

story.for_you: You hold your phone near a reader at a shop, a train gate or a car door. It works if the bank or key app has been allowed to do it. You do not need to open Apple Wallet or Google Wallet.
story.for_makers: A bank or car maker can run its own tap experience and brand it. This avoids sharing the experience with the system wallet. Apple only opened this widely after European law and later in more countries.

use_cases.example: A bank wallet app takes a tap at a shop without using Apple Pay.
A city transit app lets riders tap through the gate with a pass held in the app.
A car maker's app unlocks a vehicle when you hold your phone to the door handle.
An office badge in a company app opens doors and checks you in.
A store app holds loyalty and payment in one tap.
A student ID opens dorm doors.
A hotel app holds a room key that expires at check out.

story.android_note: Android has let apps emulate a card in software (host card emulation) since 2013, with no approval from Google needed.
story.ios_note: Apple first opened this in the EU with iOS 17.4 and added the NFC and secure chip APIs in more countries from iOS 18.1.

history.change: HCE for contactless payments in the EU
NFC and SE APIs in more regions
